candidates.title: [Bug]: compiler crashes (index out of range [-1]) on a function type with an unnamed parameter before a defaultable parameter
candidates.body:
### Description
A function type descriptor where an unnamed parameter comes before a defaultable parameter crashes the compiler.

- As a module-level type definition, the compiler dies with an uncaught Go panic: `panic: runtime error: index out of range [-1]`, from `projects/package_compilation.go:174`.
- As a local variable's type, it reports `fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: panic during desugaring: runtime error: index out of range [-1]`.

When it happens:
- `function (int a, int b = 3)`, where every parameter before the default is named, works and prints `2` and `4`.
- `function (int a = 3, int = 4)` also works.
- Any unnamed parameter before a defaultable one crashes, e.g. `function (int, int b = 3)` or `function (int = 3, int b = 4)`.

The likely cause is that building the default's closure looks up the earlier parameters by name, and the unnamed one gives index -1. This is not verified in the code.

Spec (function types, param-list):
- `required-param := [annots] type-descriptor [param-name]`
- "A param-name can be omitted from a required-param, defaultable-param, included-record-param or rest-param only when occuring in the function-signature of a function-type-descriptor."

So the program is valid. A compiler crash is a bug in any case.

### Steps to Reproduce
Run `bal run` on:
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

type F function (int, int b = 3) returns int;

function add(int x, int y) returns int => x + y;

public function main() {
    F f = add;
    io:println(f(1, 1)); // @output 2
    io:println(f(1)); // @output 4
}
```

- **Expected:** prints `2` then `4`.
- **Actual:**
```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [-1]

goroutine 1 [running]:
github.com/ballerina-nutcracker/ballerina/projects.(*PackageCompilation).compileModulesInternal(...)
	.../projects/package_compilation.go:174 +0xfab
```

Local-variable variant:
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

function add(int x, int y) returns int => x + y;

public function main() {
    function (int, int b = 3) returns int f = add;
    io:println(f(1, 1)); // @output 2
    io:println(f(1)); // @output 4
}
```

This gives `fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: panic during desugaring: runtime error: index out of range [-1]`.

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ a0d9acbe902af2c526594e49ec6a8b9140574ecc

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux x86_64, Go 1.24.7 (toolchain go1.27.1), `go run ./cli/cmd run <file>`

### Related area
Compilation

### Related issue(s) (optional)
Possibly related: #1227, #1232 (function-type defaults referring to parameters), PR #1534 (default-param closures built from the earlier params).

### Suggested label(s) (optional)
Type/Bug

candidates.title: [Bug]: lexer treats non-ASCII characters as hex digits (INTERNAL_ERROR on `0x1Ł`, invalid `\u{Ł}` escape accepted)
candidates.body:
### Description
When the lexer checks for a hex digit, it truncates the code point to its low byte (`isHexDigit(byte(reader.Peek()))` in `parser/lexer.go`, in `processHexLiteral` and `processNumericEscapeWithoutBackslash`).

So any character whose low byte is an ASCII hex digit counts as a hex digit. For example, `Ł` is U+0141, and its low byte 0x41 is `A`. This has three effects:

1. **Compiler crash:** `int i = 0x1Ł;` gives `fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: failed to parse numeric literal`. `io:println(0xŁ);` does the same.
2. **Invalid string escape accepted:** `"\u{Ł}"` compiles and evaluates to the six characters `\u{Ł}`.
3. **Invalid identifier escape accepted:** `int \u{Ł} = 1;` compiles.

Spec (lexical structure):
- `HexDigit := Digit | a .. f | A .. F`
- `HexIntLiteral := HexIndicator HexNumber`
- `HexNumber := HexDigit+`
- `StringNumericEscape := \u{ CodePoint }`
- `CodePoint := HexDigit+`

`Ł` is not a HexDigit. So `0x1Ł` must lex as `0x1` followed by a stray token (an ordinary syntax error), and `\u{Ł}` is not a valid escape, so it must be a compile error.

### Steps to Reproduce
Crash:
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    // U+0141 (Ł) is not a hex digit, but its low byte is 0x41 (A)
    int i = 0x1Ł; // @error
    io:println(i);
}
```

- **Expected:** a normal syntax error on line 5.
- **Actual:** `fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: failed to parse numeric literal`

Wrongly accepted string escape:
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    // U+0141 (Ł) is not a hex digit, but its low byte is 0x41 (A)
    io:println("\u{Ł}"); // @error
}
```

- **Expected:** a compile error.
- **Actual:** compiles and prints `\u{Ł}`.

Wrongly accepted identifier escape:
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    int \u{Ł} = 1; // @error
    io:println(\u{Ł});
}
```

- **Expected:** a compile error.
- **Actual:** compiles and prints `1`.

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ a0d9acbe902af2c526594e49ec6a8b9140574ecc

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux x86_64, Go 1.24.7 (toolchain go1.27.1), `go run ./cli/cmd run <file>`

### Related area
Parser

### Related issue(s) (optional)
Related:
- #1054: the same `failed to parse numeric literal` INTERNAL_ERROR, but caused by an out-of-range literal.
- #1348 / PR #1359: fixed surrogate and out-of-range `\u{}` escapes, but kept the `byte(reader.Peek())` truncation.

### Suggested label(s) (optional)
Type/Bug

candidates.title: [Bug]: methods named `map`, `join` or `start` are rejected with a syntax error
[Bug]: `toString()`/`toBalString()` method call on an object-typed receiver gives "method not found"
candidates.body:
### Description
If the receiver's static type is an object type and the object has no method with that name, a method call does not fall back to the `lang.value` langlib function.

`q.toString()` and `q.toBalString()` give `SEMANTIC_ERROR: method not found: toString` / `toBalString`. The explicit calls `value:toString(q)` and `value:toBalString(q)` compile, and so does `a.toString()` when `a` is typed `any`. Only object-typed receivers are affected. A class that defines its own `toString()` still can't call `p.toBalString()`.

Spec §6.16 (method call expression):
- A method-call-expr calls an object method or a function-typed field only if the object type has a member named method-name.
- "Otherwise, the method-call-expr will be turned into a call to a function in the lang library m:method-name(expression, arg-list) ... If the static type of expression is a subtype of some basic type with identifier B, and the module lang.B contains a function method-name then M is B. ... Otherwise, M is value."
- `lang.object` has no `toString`/`toBalString`, so M is `value`.

subset10 lists `value:toString` and `value:toBalString` among the langlib functions callable with method-call syntax, and does not exclude object receivers.

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;
import ballerina/lang.value;

class Plain {
    int x = 1;
}

public function main() {
    Plain q = new;
    // Plain has no toString/toBalString method, so per spec 6.16 these
    // method calls resolve to value:toString(q) / value:toBalString(q).
    io:println(q.toString() == value:toString(q)); // @output true
    io:println(q.toBalString() == value:toBalString(q)); // @output true
}
```

- **Expected:** prints `true` twice.
- **Actual:**
```
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: method not found: toString
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: method not found: toBalString
```

### Affected Version(s)
`main` @ a0d9acbe902af2c526594e49ec6a8b9140574ecc

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux x86_64, Go 1.24.7 (toolchain go1.27.1), `go run ./cli/cmd run <file>`

### Related area
Type checker

### Related issue(s) (optional)
Related:
- PR #838 (fall back to lang.value in method-call resolution): it doesn't cover object receivers.
- #979, #1511: how objects are rendered by toString. The reproducer avoids that issue by comparing the two forms instead of printing.

### Suggested label(s) (optional)
Type/Bug

candidates.title: [Bug]: default expressions in function type descriptors are not type-checked or isolation-checked

notes:
Stopped at the limit of 5 confirmed candidates (about 20 minutes into the run). Two of them are compiler crashes and were not spec-validated, per policy; the other three were confirmed against the master spec by separate validation subagents. All 5 were checked against existing issues and PRs with REST search and are new.

Dropped because they are already filed:
- query select closure capture: #1093
- readonly-typed query result: #1149
- is/cast on T&readonly lists and maps ignores shape: #1044
- cast away error accepted: #1332
- unary -/~ keep int subtype: #1046
- no singleton typing for * / % shift bitwise: #1262
- XML template entity refs not decoded without interpolation: #1091
- xmlns="" rejected in XML template: #1226
- compile-time singleton folding overflow: #1492 / #1096

Dropped as not a bug: computed-name field overwriting a readonly field during mapping construction. Spec §6.7.2 sets the read-only bit only after construction, and maintainers settled this on PR #1193.

Unreported observations:
- `xml[i]` member access is rejected with 'unsupported container type for index based access'. It may be unimplemented rather than a bug.
- Object type tests appear to use declared field types rather than shapes (the spec is ambiguous here).
- `0.0d` prints as `0`, which is deliberate in decimal.FormatBallerina.
